utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Before we hear the next witness, are there any matters the parties would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karnavas, are there any protective measures for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: None, Your Honour, none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So we can start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And we'd like to welcome back Judge Vassylenko. We're glad to have you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Mr. Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. The witness is yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us your name.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: My name is Desimir Bucalina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us your last name letter by letter.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: B-U-C with a diacritic -A-L-I-N-A.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't think you need to hold the headset. It will stay on. There you go. Just relax. July 1995, were you a member of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please tell us in which unit you were serving.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I was a member of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where exactly were you positioned?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: At the Zuti Most checkpoint near Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long had you been at that post, sir?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: From 1994 to the end, that means the 18th of March, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was there a commanding officer, a komandir, that was at the Zuti Most while you were serving there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. It was Jovan Ivic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What was your relationship, and I'm speaking work-wise, with the commander of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I did not have any contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You did not report to him?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who did you report to?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Jovo, as head of the checkpoint, related all the information regarding the work of the checkpoint to Captain Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when Jovo -- and we're speaking of -- who also has the name the Russian, Rus, Ivic, when he was not there, who would you report to directly?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Jovo worked at the checkpoint every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If Momir Nikolic was not there, who would you report to or who would Jovo report to?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: You mean in relation to reports about the work of the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: If a problem occurred regarding the operation of the checkpoint, he sought approval from superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When you say "superior command," we have to be precise here. Are we speaking about the superior command of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No. All information regarding the passage of convoys we received from the headquarters in the corps command, and they were in charge of all the information, the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. To what extent was the commander of the Bratunac Brigade involved in matters related to convoys or passage through the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No, he was not at all involved in the population of Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please explain to us, when you say "control," what exactly do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: When I say "control" or checking of convoys, I mean this: We received in advance an overview of the passage of convoys in and out of the enclave, so we checked the number of people, the equipment they were carrying, and the freight on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, this advance overview, would that be similar to a manifest, a bill of lading?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Where would you receive this advance overview from?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: From the Main Staff of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how would you compare the advance overview, this document that you had, with the -- the convoy itself? If you could be as concrete as you could.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: When the convoy would come in, we would know exactly how many people were coming in, the time of arrival and departure, and the contents of what they were carrying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you check the contents of the convoy?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What if inside the convoy there were contents that were not reflected on the advance overview or were contents deemed as contraband? What would you do then?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Jovo, as the leader of the checkpoint, would find Mr. Nikolic, and Mr. Nikolic then decided how to deal with the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, these convoys, from before arriving to the Zuti Most, from how many different checkpoints would they be coming from?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Depending on whether they were arriving via Yugoslavia or from Kiseljak. If they were coming via Yugoslavia, there was a checkpoint in Karakaj, Zvornik, and in most cases the convoys were escorted by the military police from Zvornik, and the checks were only routine on our part because they were not allowed to pile up. They had come under escort anyway. And if they were coming from Kiseljak, I don't know if there were any other checkpoints before Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I want to go step-by-step and I would like you to slow down because it makes it easier for the translation. So if it's coming from Yugoslavia, the first checkpoint would be Karakaj; correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it from your experience in these matters that was -- the contents would be controlled, matched, that is, with the advance overview, this manifest, versus what was in the convoy itself. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, unless they were convoys under the escort of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me -- let me make sure that I -- I want to go step-by-step. I'm speaking about Karakaj now. When the convoy comes in at Karakaj --

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- are you saying there were some convoys that were under the escort of military police, or are you saying that after leaving Karakaj the convoy would be escorted by military police toward the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. The escort of the military police was from Karakaj to Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. To make sure that I'm clear with my former question, when the convoy would come in from Yugoslavia to Karakaj, is it my understanding that at that point, at that first checkpoint, the convoy would be controlled? In other words, the manifest checked with the contents of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then if there was a military escort with that convoy, upon arrival at the Zuti Most it would be more or less a pro forma checking and off the convoy would go?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. For a while Mr. Karnavas has been leading, and that's just the latest example of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying to clear the matter, but that's okay, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe you have a better way to put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Once it cleared Karakaj, from there, assuming that there was a -- a military police escort, as you've testified already, once the convoy arrived at the Zuti Most, please tell us how detailed of a control or a checking of the contents of the convoy would take place at the Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: We only recorded the passage of convoys and, without detaining them, we let them through.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And that would be pro forma, then, would it not?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if the convoy came from the other direction, the other checkpoint, the other border crossing which was -- again, what was that crossing?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: From the direction of Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that -- at that particular -- with those particular convoys, to what extent would the controlling process be?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: That depended on the size of the convoy. They would stay at the checkpoint from 30 minutes to 90 minutes, depending on how long it took to inspect them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: As part of the controlling process, did you have authority to prevent goods for humanitarian aid to go into the enclave?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No, not if their papers were in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If the papers were in order, were you allowed to take goods out? In other words, to try to starve the people in Srebrenica? You know, engage in convoy terrorism, as some may have suggested on previous occasions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, what kind of question are you asking this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think this is just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's very suggestive, very suggestive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you or did you at any point in time take out foodstuffs, humanitarian aid, from the convoys so that those goods could not reach their intended destinations?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you ever ordered by Colonel Blagojevic to do that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about Momir Nikolic; did he ever order you to do that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, speaking about Momir Nikolic, what was his rank?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: He had the rank of captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How was he addressed in front of the Dutch Battalion, his counterparts?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: He told us then when Dutch soldiers were around the checkpoint, we should address him as Major Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you address him as Major Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, although it was Jovo who did most of the talking with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it the purpose for addressing him as a major in front of the Dutch was to give the impression to his Dutch counterparts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I mean, it's obvious that's a leading question. I mean, everyone in this courtroom knows what the purpose is in this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think this question is necessary. Or you maybe find another way to put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think I made the point. I got the reaction which was intended, Your Honour. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If counsel is acknowledging that he's deliberately asking improper questions in order to bait the Prosecution, I think something should be done about that. And that's exactly what he's done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, Mr. McCloskey. Mr. Karnavas, I think the question you ask has a point, but the problem is that you don't have to bring any other things into the contents of your question, especially those could be -- if they offend the other party.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it shouldn't offend the other party since they've claimed he was an honest and truthful witness. That was before they had this other witness who also allegedly perjured himself. So these are the points that I'm trying to make, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's a false statement. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just -- this issue has been over and over and over again. Mr. Nikolic admitted this, and the liaison officers in the VRS did this constantly, as do security and intel. people in armies everywhere. This and many of the other issues we're seeing have been done over and over and over again. We haven't said anything about that, but when it comes to deliberately baiting the lawyers, and, "Oh, I got the reaction," this kind of unprofessional, childlike attitude is just demeaning the courtroom and it's -- I just don't know what else to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the whole purpose was to demonstrate how the Prosecution continually tries to protect Mr. Nikolic. Mr. Nikolic was able to convince the whole world that he was a major. In other words, he is a clever -- I don't know what other word to use, you know. I mean, he is clever in being dishonest and he was able to sell his dishonesty to the Prosecution and the Prosecution has been trying to sell it to the Tribunal, and that's what I'm trying to demonstrate, and when they get the reactions because it hurts them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is absolutely outrageous what this man continues to say. He should be told to sit down and stop it. You know, this is a dead issue, and for him to just continually -- he wants me to get down in the mud with him, and I will try to resist it. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's a good choice. Mr. Karnavas, I think we have come across this issue for many times in the past, and you have already made your point there. The problem is not to persuade the Prosecution. The problem is to let us to understand your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that anything that's overdone will do harm to your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I want to talk about -- focus your attention on July 1995, and I would like to focus your attention on a narrow period, July 6 being the day when the events concerning Srebrenica commenced, July 11th we know is a fixed day, is when Srebrenica fell. So starting with July 6, on or about that period did you, sir, receive any special instructions, orders, or information about any events concerning Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. From where you were located on the 6th of July, did you notice any troop movement, any soldiers coming through the Zuti Most to try to attack, for instance, the DutchBat, or try to capture Potocari or advance towards Srebrenica from that direction?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, what about the 7th? Were there --

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the 8th?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What about the 9th?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. July 10th?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Could you please tell us about what time it would have been on the 10th that you noticed something unusual, and then you'll describe to us what it was you noticed.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Sometime in the evening, it could have been 7.00 or 8.00 p.m., a group of men in camouflage uniforms whom I didn't know arrived. I later learned they were members of the special police unit of the MUP of Republika Srpska. They stayed for about 15 or 20 minutes at the checkpoint, consulting or reaching an agreement about the operation of that unit for the next day, for the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. First of all, did you recognise these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I recognised one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who it was that you recognised.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: It was Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you know him from before?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, do you know whether the men that were there were there with Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: They were with him, but I don't know these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So they were -- all right. You did not recognise any of them being from -- from the Bratunac area?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they come up to the Zuti Most to give any orders or make any requests?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No, they did not. They did not talk to us at all. They stood close to the Zuti Most checkpoint, and they were consulting, conferring about something, but they were not issuing any orders concerning us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That particular night, July 10th, where do you spend?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: At the Zuti Most checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on the 11th, the day that Srebrenica fell, were you there at the Zuti Most the entire day?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I was at Zuti Most sometime up until 11.00. I don't remember exactly, but it was when Captain Nikolic left one person at the checkpoint at Zuti Most, whereas the three of us left for Potocari on the mission of helping the evacuation, at least that's what Nikolic hold us, of the civilian population that was supposed to go to the territory held by the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me stop you here. Now, I'm speaking about the 11th of July. On that particular day, we know Srebrenica fell, and we know the following day that buses arrived in Potocari. So that when -- in speaking about the day that Nikolic asked you to go into Potocari, was that the day that the buses arrived, or was it the day before the buses arrived?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Nikolic told us to go on the first day of the evacuation, when the evacuation started.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So that would be the 12th. But the preceding day --

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The preceding day, did you see anything unusual on that day at the Zuti Most; any fighting, any advancement of troops, any attacking of the Dutch Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: On the 11th, a unit of the special police started, set off from the direction of Zuti Most towards the UNPROFOR base, but I don't know if there was any fighting. I don't think there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice any de-mining going on at that area?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No. Only in the morning one of the members of the special unit came across a mine to the right of the Zuti Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And was that that day, the 11th, the day before the evacuation process?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, the 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on the 12th -- by the way, on the 11th where did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I spent the night of the 11th at the Zuti Most checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 12th now, would you please tell us where you were in the morning.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: At the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated earlier that Momir Nikolic came sometime in the morning; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us when he came what, if anything, did he say?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: He told us that Jovan Ivic was to remain at the checkpoint, and the remaining three men should set off towards Potocari in order to secure an unhindered passage of the people who were supposed to be evacuated to the territory under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did Momir Nikolic at that point in time express the importance of his position, if indeed he held one at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did he ever say that he had been -- he was to be the coordinator of this entire event that was going on in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you got to Potocari, could you please tell us, first of all, how far did you go? Because we understand Potocari is a rather large area.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: We came behind the UNPROFOR base headquartered at the battery factory, across the Faros factory. So the distance between the gates of these two factories was about 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when you got there, could you please tell us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: There was a cordon of the Dutch Battalion members, and behind them was a mass, a huge crowd of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what were you instructed to do once you got there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Nothing. Just to provide a secure exit and to prevent any problems from occurring while those people were boarding the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, who gave you those instructions?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where was it when he gave you these instructions? Where were you located?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: When he came to the checkpoint and took us to Potocari, he told us what our mission was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, how did you know where to stand?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: He told us to join the Dutch soldiers who were standing in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How far were you from the Dutch soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: We were right next to them. In fact, we were in the same line with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that you were doing the same thing that the Dutch soldiers were doing?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you ever told to abuse anyone over there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see the Dutch soldiers abusing anyone over there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you see any VRS, members of the VRS, or members of the MUP abusing anyone while you were over there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, how long were you in Potocari standing next to the Dutch soldiers?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Approximately until the afternoon, by which time a considerable number of people left Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before we speak about what you did next, could you please tell us, when you were in Potocari, did you see any higher echelon officers there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: There were officers, but the only man that I recognised was General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How close were you to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Not very far. He passed by me when he came to address the civilians, and he was some 15 or 20 metres away from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you able to hear what General Mladic was saying to the civilians there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you believe General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you said at some point that you were -- you said earlier that you were at this line next to the Dutch, performing the same duties that the Dutch were doing up until early afternoon. Could you please tell us, where did you go after that? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I went closer to the centre of Potocari, which is some 100 -- 200 metres from the point where the factory compound was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what was the purpose for moving your position, going to that area?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note we didn't get the name of the factory.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An acquaintance of mine told me that in that area my direct superior from the company where I worked and my high school professor was, and I simply wanted to see that woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. First of all, what was the name of the factory that you indicated earlier?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Where this woman was?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. You indicated you went closer to the centre. So what was the name of the factory that you went to? We need it for the record.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: The galvanising factory, the compound of the galvanising factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you receive an order from anyone to leave your position, where you were next to the Dutch, and to go searching for your former director and former professor from high school?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No. Nobody told me anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you find the woman?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us her name.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Dzevahira Maric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Maric or Paric?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Paric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us with whom she was.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: She was with her husband, a son who was 13 or 14 years old, and a two-year-old daughter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you speak to her?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Would you please describe to us what exactly the two of you spoke about.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: We talked as acquaintances and friends about everything. She asked about my family, where they were, what they were doing, and she asked me, if possible, to go to her house - she gave me the key - and to collect her family albums and to bring them to her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did she ask you any other questions?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Given that she had heard General Mladic's speech, she told me that she didn't want to separate from her husband, and she wanted to know what she was supposed to do in such situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you give her any advice or any suggestions?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I just told her that if she wanted to leave the enclave together with him, then she should spend the night in Potocari and to leave together on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why did you give her that advice?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I don't know what else I could have told her. She simply didn't want to separate from him. So what other option was there? That was the only way for them to travel together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you told her to just stay overnight and then the following day go with her husband, why were you suggesting that she spend the night there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Because it was a known fact that the whole evacuation could not have been completed in one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Why not suggest to her to go with her husband on that day, the first day, to try to get on the bus to leave?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: The evacuation was nearly over. I don't know exactly by which time it went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, when you told her to wait until the following day to board the bus with her husband, did you believe what you were telling her?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I absolutely did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did she ask anything else from you other than seeing if you could go to her house and take her photo album?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Already in the afternoon, I don't know who organised bread and water to be brought in, I gave her bread, but she asked me if I could supply her with cigarettes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you find the bread?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Bread was brought from Bratunac in trucks, and it was distributed to the people there in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, could you please tell us about what time you left Potocari that day.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I can't say exactly. It could have been at around 5.30 or 6.00 p.m. or within that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: To the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where did you spend the night?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: At the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That afternoon while you were at the Zuti Most or going back to the Zuti Most, did you notice any vehicles with only men in them?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you got to the Zuti Most, were buses and trucks still heading towards Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I believe that for that day the evacuation was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. The day that you were there, did you see any men being separated from their families, physically separated?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you notice whether any men were being taken to a -- a house, sort of a white house, as a collection point? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No, I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, on the 13th, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: On the evening of the 12th, a man from the checkpoint went to Bratunac because we didn't have facilities to sleep at the checkpoint, and I asked him to go to my home and bring me cigarettes and some candies, because on the day before that my professor's daughter had asked for some candies, and I promised to bring them on the following day. On the morning, he brought what I asked for, and sometime in the morning I went again to Potocari and gave a pack -- pack of cigarettes to her and some candies or cakes, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me clarify one point. You said, "We did not have facilities to sleep at the Zuti Most." I believe that's what you just stated.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Earlier you'd been telling us that you'd been staying there overnight for several days.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, but our internal agreement was that each one of us four would go in the evening to change, to take a bath, and to bring whatever we needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it on that particular day, the night of the 12th, it was this gentleman's turn to go into Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Well, we had an internal agreement. There was no particular order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next day, on the 13th, when you went to Potocari with the cigarettes and the candy to give to your former director and former professor, did you have permission to go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I didn't ask anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On that day, did Momir Nikolic show up to give orders to you or to others to go into Potocari to continue to work next to DutchBat, standing side by side, separating the crowd, seeing that they're getting onto the buses in a safe manner?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, the appropriate question would be did he continue to do the same as he did the day before, but this is certainly a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's not leading, Your Honour, because, first of all, he's already testified to this, and all I'm doing is looping. It's a perfectly legitimate technique where you take an already-given answer from the witness and you make it a form of the next question. It is factually correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think the problem is about your characterisation of the manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's exactly what he said, Your Honour, that he was ordered to. I'm not saying that everything was done that way, but he was ordered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I know, I know, but it's whether the people were getting on the bus in a safe manner or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: He was ordered to do that. That's what I'm saying, that he was ordered to go and stand next to the DutchBat so that the people could get onto the buses, not that the people were getting onto the buses, but he was ordered to make sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas certainly used the word "separations," and the witness at no point said there were separations. In fact, the witness said there were no separations, and now Mr. Karnavas uses this word which, as you know, is a sensitive word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who said the word is sensitive?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think that's a different matter. Maybe, Mr. Karnavas, you should -- you should take it step-by-step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll just rephrase, Your Honour. I think it might be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, rephrase it step-by-step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just remind us, the previous day, what was the concrete order that you had been given by Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Are you referring to the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The 12th.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: The order was, therefore, that we should be there together with the Dutch in order to prevent any commotion while people were getting on the buses and trucks. That was the only order we received.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. On the 13th did you receive a similar order?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether Momir Nikolic ordered others?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone else from the Zuti Most went back to Potocari to continue the tasks that had been ordered to them the previous day by Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 13th, sir, after you went back and you met with your former professor, former director, gave her the cigarettes, gave her child the candy, did you notice whether her husband was with her on that day, on that morning when you were there?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How long did you spend with them on that day?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Not too long. Maybe ten or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what did you do after that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I returned to the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to go back a little bit and fill in a little gap. On the night of the 12th to the 13th, was there a convoy or a truck that was parked or that was stopped at the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: On the morning between 12th and the 13th -- or, rather, the night between those two days, a truck remained at the checkpoint, and I know that there was one man in the truck, but I'm not aware if there were other men. And he was the man who had received medical treatment in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. When Jovo was there, the commanding officer of the checkpoint, who would liaison with the counterparts, the Dutch? Who among you?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: You mean in those particular days or in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In general. Who would be responsible? Would each of you be speaking, acting as a liaison officer with them or was there one spokesperson dealing with the Dutch?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Jovo was the one, because he spoke a little English, and he arranged meetings between Captain Nikolic, or if they requested a meeting with Captain Nikolic, he was the one who carried the messages to and fro.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On that day, on the 13th, did you see Captain Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. On that day, did you spend the night at the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: On the night of the 13th I did not spend at Zuti Most. I went home to take a bath and change.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us, how did you get home?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I walked from Zuti Most to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where is your house located?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: It is very close to the command, across the Kaolin factory in Bratunac, some 200 metres from the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, for those of us who haven't been to -- to Bratunac, as you leave Potocari and you're heading towards Bratunac, there's an intersection before you have to turn, make a left turn to head on toward where the command post is, and that road takes you on to -- towards Konjevic Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At that intersection, am I correct in noting that as you go around the intersection, almost right there, right across is the Hotel Fontana?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes, on the right-hand side of the junction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, did you take that route on that night?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Why not?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Because there's a shortcut before this curve, and it's a shorter way to get home.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That shortcut, I take it you would still have to at some point make a left turn to take that shortcut; correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. This street goes to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And in fact, if we were to go there today, we would find some shopping malls back there; butcher shops, I believe there's a bakery over there as well at that location, hairdresser.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: The shopping mall was constructed there with all these shops that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the distance between where you would turn off to take the shortcut to where the corner is located -- the intersection is located, what are we talking about? How many metres are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Approximately 200 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we were to follow the road itself, take the intersection and head towards -- towards the Kaolin factory where the Bratunac Brigade headquarters were, could you please tell us where the Vuk -- the Vuk Karadzic school, or the school that was then called Vuk Karadzic, was located? Would it be on the left side or the right side of the road?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: On the right side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it's not right on the road, is it?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, there's some distance to it.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Perhaps some 500, 600 metres. Maybe even more, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On that night when you went home taking that shortcut, did you notice any buses or trucks full of Muslim males?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you become aware on that night that there were Muslim males being held either in buses or trucks or the Vuk Karadzic school, for instance?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: When you turn into this street on my way home, I was stopped by one of the members of the military police. I didn't know this young man, boy; he was shorter than me. He told me, anyway, that we needed to go to town to guard some people. I said I didn't want to do that, I was going home to get some rest, and I went on my way. Later on I learned that there were some people, but how many and what it was all about, I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, why didn't you want to go and guard? Was there any other -- did you say anything else to this gentleman?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. The entire platoon of the military police was replaced in April 1994 because two detainees had been taken out of our detention unit. And referring to that, I said if I was unable to guard two Muslims in our own detention centre, then I don't want to participate in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And incidentally, the two Muslims that were guarded, that was at the detention right by the Bratunac Brigade military police; correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. In the same building, the building of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How, with all those military police under the watchful eye of Momir Nikolic, did they escape?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is leading. I mean, even earlier, you could have asked "Where was this detention centre?" and the witness could have answered in his own words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying to shorten the period, and I think we've had testimony already that there was -- you know, even from previous witnesses, that that's where they were, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where was -- where was the detention centre?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: It was right near the entrance of the building of the military police. The right-hand side, there was a room where they were, the detainees, and opposite their room was the place of the duty officer, the duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What happened to these detainees?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I would like to know too, but I just did not manage to find out. With the fall of Srebrenica, people got hold of certain papers where some details were indicated, including the way they got out and other things that I did not get access to. But I know that their departure was organised. They were practically not really detained. They were in a room without bars on the windows; it was not a typical prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was Momir Nikolic still in charge of security and intelligence at that time?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And were you a member of the military police at that time?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I was deputy commander of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what happened to you as a result of the vanishing of these two so-called prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: They wanted to arrest the policemen who were on duty that night, but since they were absolutely convinced that none of the military police had a hand in it, we did not allow the arrest of those men, and we wanted clarification. We wanted the truth to come out. However, a Solomon solution was found after a tug-of-war that lasted about ten days, and the platoon of the military police in that composition was disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And where were you sent?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Considering that the zone of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade covered three battalions, people tried to stay closer to home, and a solution was found wherein some people would go to the 1st and the 2nd Battalion, whereas the 3rd Battalion was a problem because it was the most remote from Bratunac and nobody wanted to go there. And to stop all this agony that lasted ten to 15 days, I said I would go, and then another four or five policemen came with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How was it that you got back to being a military police officer since you were basically dismissed from your position, if I understand you correctly.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just say one thing: Even after the military police platoon was disbanded, an offer was made to me to stay in the military police, and I left, together with the other soldiers. And to avoid the continuation of this problem, Momir Nikolic put me back on the checkpoint, but this time he told me I would do only regular police business. No arrests, no detentions, just the normal police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Whose suggestion was it that you go to the Zuti Most checkpoint? Who suggested it?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Based on his suggestion, he made it possible for you to just be there at the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: It must have been an agreement with the commander of the 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now that we covered that little detour, let's go back to the 13th. On the morning -- you said you spent the night at home on the 13th. On the morning of the 14th did you notice any buses or trucks in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sometime after the fall of Srebrenica - September, October - we've heard testimony that there was this rather significant activity going on with respect to a reburial process. Were you at any point in time asked to assist in those activities?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, getting back to your former professor and former director, the woman that you gave bread to on the one day, on the 12th, and then went back to give cigarettes and candy to her children, she'd asked you to go to her house, gave you the key for you to go to her house in Srebrenica to look for the photo album. Did you do that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, could you please tell us about when it was that you went into Srebrenica to locate her house.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think it could have been on the 15th or the 16th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you able to locate the photo album?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No. When I arrived, the house had already been opened, and there was no electricity in the basement, where she said the photo albums were, and I was unable to find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. What did you do with the keys to the house?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: The keys to the house, I gave them to Mr. Petko Rakic, who, after the fall of Srebrenica went to the Srebrenica Crisis Staff. But I told him, since all the villages around Srebrenica were destroyed, that that house should be given to somebody for use, for temporary use, to accommodate somebody, because -- until we see what to do with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you ever have contact again with this woman?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. She called me in the autumn of 1995. She called me on the phone at home, and she was making inquiries about her husband and son. I didn't see her husband and son in Potocari, but she said they had not reached Tuzla, and she wanted to know if I knew anything. I said I didn't know anything, and if I had known, I would have told her because she deserved that much. I just told her when she said that there were some people in the mine of Sase, I told her it wasn't true, but I had no other information to give her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Let me stop you here, because at least on the translation here it says that you did not see her -- her husband and son in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did you see her husband on the 12th and the 13th when you went to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You also indicated that she had a son with her at the time, and I believe you thought he was 12 or 13 years old, somewhere in that ballpark age.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was that the same husband and the same son that she was making inquiries about?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well -- well, let's take it step-by-step. It was the same husband she was talking about?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But I take it it was a different son that she was asking about.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How well did you know this family?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Very well. I knew them from when we were in school until 1992. They were even guests at my wedding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, when she made this inquiry and you indicated to her that you didn't have any information, did you try to find any information for her to see whether you could locate or learn what had happened to her husband and to her one son?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I tried through people who participated in the transport of the civilian population. However, I was unable to find out anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, before we go into any more details with respect to the efforts that you made and the contacts that you've had with this -- this woman, I believe it might be time for a break, and I don't have much more, just so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. If you request --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will have our break, and we will resume at quarter to eleven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, before we left off, we were speaking about you having been contacted by your former director, former professor, the woman that you had seen in Potocari on the 12th and the 13th. Do you recall about when, what year it was that she contacted you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And how was that contact made?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: She found my home telephone number and called me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And did you meet with her on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No. When I answered the phone, she told me that if I was expecting to have any problems because of that telephone conversation, that I should hang up, and she was hoping that I didn't change in the meantime and that our relationship hadn't changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, why would she think that you might have some problems because of a telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Maybe she thought that my telephone was bugged and that it could be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you eventually meet with her?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. When I started to work in Srebrenica, I'm not sure any more whether it was in 1997, 1998, or 1999, but I met up with her.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And what was the nature of the meeting at that point?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: We just talked. She inquired about my family, what we were doing, how we were doing. It was an informal conversation. We didn't go back to 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it that her husband and her son are still missing.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to go back, take you back a little bit to the 12th of July. Here this woman had come to you, or you had -- you had met with her, and had asked you what to do, and you had given her some advice, that is to stay overnight and as a family go in the next day to wherever the buses were going. How did you feel, knowing that perhaps you had given her the wrong advice?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: What can I say? I thought it was the only thing I could tell her at the time. But later on, when I found out her husband and son were missing, I had a hard time, especially during our encounter after 1995, because - how can I say this? - it's a family tragedy. I didn't have the heart to tell her. I didn't know what to tell her. Whatever I said would be superfluous.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to switch to just a couple of other matters. I'm going to hit some topics very quickly so we can wrap it up. Just going back to those two prisoners that we talked about earlier, the ones that were at the Bratunac Brigade facility back in 1994. I just want to make sure that we're clear. Were they taken away to be executed?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where were they taken away to?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: To the territory under the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And am I correct in noting that in light of what happened afterwards, that is people getting dismissed, the ongoing investigation of who was responsible and what have you, that this was sort of mysteriously done?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, we spoke a little bit about Momir Nikolic. Did you -- were you ever contacted by his lawyers? This is when Momir Nikolic was still --

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you give them a statement?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I have the statement here in front of me. It's dated 15 April 2003. Would that be about the time that you received the statement -- that you gave the statement?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on April 15, 2003, do you recall what the lawyers were asking you, what sort of information they wanted you to provide in a statement for them to give to the Office of the Prosecution or to the Court in relation to Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In your statement, do you recall being asked any information as to whether Momir Nikolic organised or coordinated the evacuation of the civilians from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fact, that was concretely asked of you, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This was back on April 15, 2003, a date that might become significant at the closing argument. Now, could you please tell us what you told his lawyers and what they took down as a statement back then with respect to Momir Nikolic being an organiser or coordinator of the evacuation of the civilians from Potocari.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I think I said he was not the one who was able to plan, organise, and do all that. It was an order from the superior command. And when I say "superior command," that means the Main Staff and the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you expressed that opinion he did not organise or coordinate the evacuation, what was that opinion based on?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I know Captain Nikolic rather well. I got to know him rather well in 1992, but I knew him even before that. In the period between 1992 and 1995, I got to know him rather well. I don't think he was able to do all that from the procurement of the means of transportation to the evacuation of the population itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Did you by any chance run into any of his lawyers that had come to you seeking such -- such a statement prior to when he changed his position? All right. You didn't hear it. Let me repeat the question. Did you run into his lawyers after you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. I did come across a man who brought me into contact with his Defence counsel. It was Stanko Petrovic from Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And in fact, that's one of the individuals whose name is on the statement that you signed, is it not?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. He was present when I gave the statement. I gave the statement in his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, was this -- was this after Momir Nikolic -- or it became known that Momir Nikolic had changed his position here in court?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, what exchange did you have with Mr. Petrovic, one of Momir Nikolic's -- one member of Momir Nikolic's Defence team? What was the exchange that you had with him with respect to the statement that they had asked you to give and in fact you had given only weeks before Momir Nikolic changed his plea?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I simply asked him what happened all of a sudden. The man who said during his plea bargain that he was not guilty, and I think he was not guilty of the job that he then admitted to having done, and he made me look like somebody who, when giving the statement, was not telling the truth, whereas I knew exactly what happened, and the answer was that he didn't know. The lawyer didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. In light of your experience being there on the ground, witnessing what you saw, knowing Momir Nikolic, his background, where he would pretend to be a major when in fact he wasn't, getting others to say he was a major when he was not, in light of all of that, when you heard what Momir Nikolic had said with respect to his activities in Potocari, did you form an opinion as to whether Momir Nikolic was being honest or dishonest with the Trial Chamber, with the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I don't think he was honest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, where have you been all these years after Srebrenica, the fall of Srebrenica, after 1995? Where are you been?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: After I was demob'd on the 18th of March, 1996, I took up my earlier job in the company where I worked before the outbreak of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where was that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: That was the social accountancy service, the development bank, the social accountancy service being the government auditing service.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. That's like a payment bureau? It's commonly referred to as the payment bureau?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And where is that located?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Just opposite the SUP building, which is the secretariat of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, but which town are we speaking about?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: In Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And incidentally, just while I'm at this, what is your level of your education?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I have completed post-secondary school of economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I notice that at one point the Office of the Prosecution did speak with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From the statement, it says that it was on 21 February 2004. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I don't remember the date, but, yes, possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It was this year?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It wasn't in 1996 or 1997 or 1998 or 1999, or 2000, 2001, 2002, 2003, it was 2004 that they were able to track you down in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Had you been asked prior to this occasion to meet with the Office of the Prosecution and you had perhaps been avoiding them, going to work incognito maybe?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No. Nobody got in touch with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did they get in touch with you on this occasion or did you learn that they were looking for you? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: They did not get in touch with me, but I heard through my friends that somebody from the Bratunac police told him that I was supposed to go and be interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so how were you interviewed?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I had expected an official summons. However, it never arrived. I quite simply went to the police station on my own will to see whether there was any need for me to go there or not. And when I asked the duty officer at the police station, he said that he didn't know either, however, but that there were the Tribunal investigators on the upper floor, so I went upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it when you went upstairs you introduced yourself.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes. The interpreter asked me if I was the person in question, and we did the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you on your own contacted them to give a statement of any potential information that you might have that might interesting to them about this case, some nine years after the incident.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in the -- what was given to us from the Office of the Prosecution, which I believe I've given you a copy of, it is literally a page and a half. I mean, if we exclude the front page. Or actually two pages, two pages. Let's be fair. Two pages. Was this interview tape recorded by any chance?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I didn't notice. If they did something, I didn't notice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it states here that the interview took place from 1500 hours to 1745 hours. That would be, if my math serves me correctly, two hours and 45 minutes, the period of which you were being questioned of which two pages of notes were generated. My first question is: Did the interview that you had gone -- gone to, did it last for two hours and 45 minutes to your recollection?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, how long do you believe or know, which of the two, this interview lasted?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I think, together with a 15-minute break, not more than one and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I seek your assistance in this issue. I fail to see the relevance of your questions to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is all I have. I don't know if anything else exists. I only have one or two more questions. I mean, the gentleman indicated to me that it didn't take -- it didn't last that long. Now, why they've represented two hours and 45 minutes when it should be an hour and a half, I don't know. We don't have a tape recorded statement. I don't know what -- what else they may produce, if anything, but I just wanted to get this detail in after the gentleman leaves in the event that some other witness shows up on rebuttal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Sometimes we got the proofing notes with only a half page, you know, and we spend two hours and three hours with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour. I agree. But I'm not the Office of the Prosecution with an armada of talent behind them, you know, and a war chest as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, try to finish your direct examination by asking two or three questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I will. But it hadn't been lost on me too that I had been submitting two-page statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In your -- in your statement, sir, I notice that there's no indication about your meeting with your former director, former professor, in Potocari on -- on that particular day. Can you give us an explanation?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Either they didn't ask me or it was not interpreted correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. That's all. I have no further questions, sir. I want that thank you very, very much for being frank and complete with me. The Prosecution will probably have some questions, no doubt, perhaps the Judges, if you could be as frank and as complete with them as you have been with me, I would most appreciate it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions to put to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. Desimir. We have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any cross-examination, Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, there will be some. And I may be using, not as an exhibit but in private session, a witness statement which we had disclosed I think back in January with this witness, and I have a courtesy copy for Mr. Karnavas which I can give to him right now, but we won't be using it in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Bucalina. It won't take too long as I just have a few issues to clarify with you. Now, first of all, when exactly did you resume or did you start your duties at the Zuti Most checkpoint? When was that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I think sometime in 1994, the autumn of 1994. I'm not sure about the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And I think you told us that the corps had control over this, controlled the checkpoint. Now, did the corps always, while you were there, have control over that checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Can you be more specific? I don't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I believe you told us this morning that it was the corps who had control over the checkpoint. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: We received papers from the corps, and the person in charge of everything that took place at the checkpoint on behalf of the brigade was Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And because you received papers from the corps, that led to your assumption that it was the corps who controlled the checkpoint; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So how would you state it then? I'm just asking you to clarify.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I said that the people who manned the checkpoint were members of the Bratunac Brigade and reported to Captain Nikolic, and he then reported further on to the corps and the corps to the staff, and vice versa, the documents travelled the opposite way, which means that all the approvals came from the Main Staff via the corps to the brigade and finally to the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, did that policy, the way you outlined it, did that change while you were there or was it always like that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: It was always like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let me go to the next issue. I believe you told us that on the 12th of July in Potocari, when you saw the crowd of people, you saw General Mladic passing behind you, I believe you said, and addressing the crowd of civilians. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now -- and Mr. Karnavas asked you whether you believed what General Mladic said, and you said absolutely. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
