utterances.text: Would you tell us what General Mladic said? So can you tell the Trial Chamber what General Mladic said that you believed as being true?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: He said that since the evacuation was not possible to be completed in one day of the whole Potocari population, and because they had to spend the night outdoors, that he was going first to send off the women and children and then the remaining population on the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the remaining population meaning including the men?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Including the men but also not all the women and children were able to leave on the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, but what you said you believed to be absolutely true was that the whole population, including the men, would be, in your words, evacuated. That was your understanding of what you heard from General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, did you hear General Mladic on TV the day before, the day he entered Srebrenica, did you hear him saying on TV --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may. If he could establish a foundation first, whether this was on TV at the time when he was at his home watching TV or whether there was a TV at the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that's necessary. You may proceed, Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mladic said on TV, and we heard it, we saw in fact a clip in this courtroom, and I quote: "The time has come to take revenge on the Turks in this region." Now, would that change your opinion of whether General Mladic had no harm in mind when he addressed the civilians as you said you had witnessed? Would that change your mind?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Probably, but I don't know about this statement of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And just a few hours before you met General Mladic, he was sitting down with representatives of the civilian population in the Hotel Fontana, and there he said, and I quote again that: "The Muslim population can 'either survive or disappear,'" and then he continued on and said if they didn't surrender, the armed men, the weapons. Now, is it again a -- of your change of opinion about the truthfulness of what General Mladic had in mind at that time?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I don't know about that, Mladic's statement, either.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But it would change your mind as what had General Mladic in mind when he addressed the civilians?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, I think you told us, or you told Mr. -- the investigator that you saw General Mladic and other people handing out food, water, candies to the civilians, including the children. Do you remember having told that to the investigator when you met with him?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, that scene was filmed, was it not?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honours, if we could play a clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if we're going to be playing a clip, in all fairness and under the rule of completeness, or the principle of completeness, it would be nice if the Prosecution would also show the gentleman the portion where Mladic is addressing the folks in Potocari, where he's telling them exactly what the gentleman heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We don't know what kind of clips that he's going to play.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's the same section, if they can find it, Your Honour. Just to be fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I think that's up to re-examination if he wants to be in broader -- I just want to show him the clip, to ask if he has seen that, and perhaps one follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If that clip could be played. It's again from Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And perhaps you could tell us if you recognise anybody.

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Who? And whom did you recognise?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: The man in the uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Ljubisa Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, are those the scene you had described, the handing out of candies? Is that what you have seen yourself?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, as you see, the scene has been filmed. Do you know what happened after the cameras were turned off?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know what the follow-up question is. We've had mixed testimony in this courtroom, and if the gentleman wants to quote from a particular witness, I don't have a problem, but if he's going to be testifying as to what happened, then he's testifying as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. Well, "what happened" is a general question. He is not leading at all. We don't know what kind of answer this witness will give us. Let us hear what the witness is going to tell us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not worried about this question, I'm worried about the follow-up, the next question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- ahead of me, I have to confess. Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Witness, the question has been, before Mr. Karnavas interfered, whether you had seen what happened after the candies were distributed to the children in front of the cameras. Have you seen what happened afterwards, after the cameras had been turned off?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: I don't know what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Let me read what's been entered into evidence in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm quoting from Witness F in Krstic, which -- whose testimony has been admitted under 92 bis as Prosecution Exhibit 781.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me tell you what a member of DutchBat said who witnessed the scene: "After the camera crew stopped filming, the general turned around. He laughed. The soldiers took the candy back, took the cigarettes back. They spit at the children and the women, and they were taken away directly." Have you seen similar scenes?

utterances.speaker: DESIMIR BUCALINA
utterances.text: No, and I think this is absurd. If you give chocolate to children, maybe the children started eating them right away. So I didn't see that, and I don't think that was true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could go for the next issue into private session because it involves witness statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, at this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Waespi?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the schedule of next week, Mr. Karnavas, the witness for next week, I suppose has been arranged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, and I thought --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We haven't received any lists for next week's witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You mean the one that's coming up, Monday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Monday. Do you have any witness today?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No. That will be it for today, Your Honour. I was under the impression that we had provided that list, but we will certainly provide a list as soon as we get out of this courtroom, because we have it ready. They have already -- some have arrived -- or, no. One is arriving. Two are arriving tomorrow. I can assure the Court that we will not run out of witnesses next week. It will be a full -- full week, and it's in fact rather doubtful that we will be able to manage all of them, but we'll do our best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But I have to remind you that especially in this week, we somehow are two or three witnesses behind our schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're well ahead of our schedule. We are, because I've taken witnesses off. I've notified, for instance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- that Mr. Nikolic, now we have P130, maybe we'll keep him in reserve for surrebuttal, but he's been taken off. But from -- from my looking at the -- at the number of witnesses that we have left, I'm rather confident that we will be able to complete on the targeted date. Now, there may be -- something may come up, because I can't forecast the future, unlike as with some questions from the Prosecution there are occasions when I have those abilities, but other than that, I can assure the Trial Chamber that we are moving in the right direction at the right pace, and I know that this week we were a little bit shy of having three witnesses or four witnesses, but I would not -- I would not worry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You never forget the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, they would feel lonely if I didn't mention them, Your Honour, and I don't want to disappoint them. They know that I love them as much as I can. It may not be a whole lot, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Next week, on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday, we have to sit in the afternoon, and on Wednesday and Thursday we'll sit in the morning. And as we discussed before, that next week we will have an extra sitting concerning with the hearings on the amendment of the indictment. Is it okay for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And do you know what date that would be?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I have to consult with the registrar about the court scheduling, and it may be Wednesday or Thursday. We might have an extra hour for that sitting. And for the sake of the record, Mr. Stojanovic, I think during this month we should also have a Pre-Defence Conference. Do you have any ideas about the time and the start of your case?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yesterday we met with Mrs. Katie Gallagher, and we agreed on the timing in principle. We still reckon that we will go according to the approved schedule in adducing our evidence, starting on Monday the 5th of July. We agreed with Mrs. Katie Gallagher that a pre-Defence conference together with the opening statements of our Defence be on the Friday of the 2nd of July, and then we would talk about the witnesses -- the list of witnesses we are proposing. We have four weeks allocated to us, ending with Friday 31st July, and it is in accordance with this schedule that we plan to bring our witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I think originally the Trial Chamber asked you to start your case on the 28th of June so that you have five weeks in your case, which is enough time. And if we start on the 5th of July for your case, you only have four weeks, exactly four weeks at your disposal. Do you think you could finish calling the witnesses before the 30th of July? I'm just worried, you know, about the time at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your concern. Yes, it's true that we were told that we could discuss starting earlier, but we have already agreed with the Victims and Witnesses Unit about the schedule of travel of witnesses. We have a final list of 14 witnesses to be heard live, plus two witnesses who will probably go under Rule 92 bis, so that we will stick to the total of 12 live witnesses. With regard to the time that we plan to take with these witnesses, I think we will fit into four weeks. If a problem arises with time, we will let the registrar and the Trial Chamber know well in advance and decide then whether we need to start before Friday the 2nd of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But the deadline is on the 30th of July. I hope you could make it to this deadline. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just a couple of issues, and I'm sure I can get together with Mr. Stojanovic to find out which witnesses he's talking about for 92 bis to determine if we will have any objections or if that will go in smoothly, because obviously that will play a role in how long that will take, and that's the first we've heard of that. Also, on -- for the Blagojevic case, we have been provided courtesy copies of expert reports for population and for military, but as far as we know, there's been no official filings under 94 bis, and so I'm hoping maybe they've decided to change their mind and not call those witnesses, but I'm sure Mr. Karnavas can clarify that for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With pleasure. Yesterday we did file a 94 -- a Rule 94, I think it's bis, motion. So -- with respect to the military expert. Even though we had provided the initial report as a courtesy copy, Mr. McCloskey had indicated that he wanted some additional information, supporting documentation. As I indicated last time we had been in court that I had anticipated that and I had been making efforts to secure that, so yesterday when we filed that, you will see two -- two attachments to this very brief motion, one being the original report, which is very limited in nature, and then a more comprehensive document which is the documentation that was relied upon in making that assessment that we presented. I'm also trying to secure the sources that are outside the record that is being referenced in the documentation that we submitted yesterday, but perhaps the Prosecution can look at that and then they can consider or reconsider their position whether they wanted to entertain a 92 bis with this particular witness or not, but I think they may need some time to look it over to let us know. With respect to the other expert, we received the expert report last Sunday, I believe, in the original, in Serbian, and we -- we did give a courtesy copy to the Office of the Prosecution because we know that they have B/C/S speakers in this very specialised unit that they have dealing with demographics. We put it on a fast track to be translated. We hope to have it translated. The report is based on information that's already contained in the -- the voluminous databank that the OTP has. This expert witness was brought to The Hague along with two assistants and spent several days going through their databank and then generated this report based on the databank and other material, but basically they have what is inclusive in this report, and much of it is a frontal attack on their expert, Mr. Brunborg [sic]. I'm hoping that this report will be -- will be translated very quickly. I do intend to call her. I would really like to call her, and I recognise that there are some time constraints, and I recognise that the Prosecution can insist, as is their right, for this 30-day period. However, you know, we are hoping that, one, that there may be a -- some solutions available. One is they can show some flexibility, as can the Court as well, or our -- our other position would be, and I -- so I'm laying my cards out, you know, at this point. Our other position would be that, one, we would end the Defence case early - early - thereby allowing the other team to proceed, and then after that we could spend -- we can bring those witnesses back after the Jokic Defence, just to clear up those two witnesses, expert witnesses, prior to the Prosecution starting their rebuttal. In doing so, the Defence will have the entire month of August at their disposal. So they certainly will not have -- plus all of July. So they will have more than enough time. So of course that's up to the Court and the Prosecution. With respect to the military expert, Mr. McCloskey's suggestion was a reasonable one, because as you will note, the assessment is on a limited basis, and that was my only -- the only basis for which I would be calling him, and I would be listing testimony solely on those narrow issues and not on the entire Srebrenica events. So I will have -- I hope that after Mr. McCloskey reads the material he will have his position, he can tell me what his position is, and then we can take it from there. So that's the best I can do at this particular time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we're talking about the love of each other here. I guess I won't go into that too much. But one thing I think I can say is that all sides have been fairly flexible in this case, which I think has been much appreciated, and in terms of logistics, things. And if we look at 94 bis, it does talk about the Prosecution does have 30 days or a time limit set by the Judge to respond to the experts. Regarding the military expert, having read the report as it stands, I really, and I'll see what else he's got, but I don't really have a problem with that coming into evidence. I don't want to accept it as fact, but have something that we can argue about, I have no problem with. We'll see what other additional information is, and if that can save us some time, that would be great. Probably do the same thing with the report on the population person, though Mr. Karnavas indicates he wants to call her. But we're open for some creative way to save that as well. I don't think these issues are -- are issues that really need a whole lot of court time, but we're of course ready to do that. So I will discuss this with Mr. Karnavas and Mr. Stojanovic, and I think we'll be able to work something out. And if I could go into private session just for a second to discuss a couple of witnesses for next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as for the expert statements and according with the Rule 94 bis, I think there's three ways to deal with, you know, this issue, and so long as the status of experts is established, normally we will admit his statement, which is different from the practice of an ordinary witness at all. In this situation, we admit the statement through 94 bis or through 92 bis, without any direct examination or cross-examination. This is the first approach. Second approach is that since we have already admitted the statement into evidence, there is some room for the cross-examination, because everything is already written there in the statement itself. We don't have to test the memory of that expert. They may be not expert in that field. So there should be no direct examination, only for the cross-examination. This is the second approach. The third approach is there might be some direct examination, but in a very limited way, just to point out the main issues in that statement, then leave much more time for the cross-examination. I think basically this is the three approach to deal with the statement of the expert witness. I hope the parties will bear that in mind. And here I would like to reiterate that the 30th of July is the last day for the Defence case for both teams. I hope the parties will take that into serious consideration. I also hope that the parties could meet together to discuss their schedule and the strategy, especially in the Defence case. Well, it seems that we have been sitting here for quite a long time, so the hearing for today is adjourned, and we will meet next Monday afternoon. Yes, Mr. Blagojevic? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BLAGOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since I see that the time is quite limited and very strictly set up, because that's what I hear from you, and since you mentioned the 30th of July, I don't see anywhere an opportunity for exercising my fundamental right, although it says it may be exercised, but I believe that under these complex circumstances, the situation is no less complicated now than it was at the time of my arrest. Please, I have the right to testify under oath before this Tribunal, and I believe that if all these written or oral statements carry weight, then my testimony should also carry certain weight in the light of this whole complex matter. I don't see that happening. I said that I have entered this stage of the proceedings totally unprepared, disoriented and uninformed, because everything is being done without my knowledge, as if I am not interested at all. However, I am very much interested, primarily because the truth that has to be uncovered in the name of justice is crucial for me too. Therefore, I wouldn't like to be pushed or remain aside for a single moment. I want to remain as much as honest as upon in this proceedings as I had been in my former life, previous life. Therefore, I would like to know what opportunities I have in this respect so that I can act accordingly. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for raising this issue again. I believe that you raised it on the previous occasions once. And I think at this stage I have to state the position of the Bench on that issue. According to the Rules, the accused could be a witness in the case, which should be entirely out of his free will. The Bench's obligation is to guarantee the right of the accused, especially of the right of not incriminating himself. Frankly speaking, at this moment the Bench take a neutral position on that. We do not encourage Mr. Blagojevic to be a witness in this case and we do not dissuade him to do that. But the issue has to be very clear here. The accused may be an expert in military affairs or the technical affairs, but the legal issue is totally different field. That's why the accused needs to have some counsels for the legal opinions. If a -- if an accused would like to be a witness in this case, I believe he has to be informed of all the rights he has and the consequences of his testimony. In this way, we strongly advise Mr. Blagojevic to consult with his counsel. I believe that Mr. Karnavas could give the professional advice to Mr. Blagojevic on this point. If there is no meeting between the -- between Mr. Blagojevic and the counsel, if Mr. Blagojevic is not well informed of all the consequences, and if there is no agreement from the counsel of Mr. Blagojevic for his testimony, the Trial Chamber will be in a very difficult position to grant the request. This is all I could say at this stage. And I think that's all for today's hearing. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of June, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.
